answer: Each epoch, influence needs an attendance proof. The network lists venues and windows; a controller must attend one event, where the organiser signs a timestamped proof for that key. A meadow fair or cedar pavilion talk counts, but one proof covers one agent at one place and time, expiring at close. Attacker cost: each fake needs its own ticket, trip and person: 350 units, 500 units travel, one day, per epoch. Forgery fails: an organiser signing absent attendees loses a 20,000-unit bond and all its proofs, and one person claiming events across an ocean in an afternoon fails the time check.
